exchange-rates-two-quotes.alt: Suppose 1 euro equals 1.25 dollars; flipped, 1 dollar equals 0.80 euro, because 1 divided by 1.25 is 0.80. When the rate changes to 1 euro equals 1.50 dollars, the euro appreciates (it buys more dollars, and a 40-euro ticket costs 60 dollars instead of 50) and the dollar depreciates (it buys about 0.67 euro instead of 0.80). Made-up rates for practice.
